Mamre
MAM-ree
proper noun
From the Hebrew, perhaps “strength” or “fatness,” the name both of an Amorite confederate of Abram and of the place that bore his name.

Biblical Definition

Mamre was the place by Hebron, marked by its oaks or terebinths, where Abram pitched his tent and dwelt and built an altar unto the LORD. It takes its name from Mamre the Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and Aner, who were confederate with Abram and joined him in the rescue of Lot from the kings of the east. Mamre became one of the chief sites of patriarchal worship and fellowship with God. There the LORD appeared unto Abraham as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day, and Abraham ran to meet the three men, entertaining the LORD and His messengers and receiving the renewed promise that Sarah should bear a son. Hard by Mamre lay the field of Machpelah with its cave, which Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite for a burying-place, and there were buried Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Jacob and Leah. Thus Mamre was bound up with the deepest mercies of the covenant: the appearing of God, the promise of the seed, the hospitality of faith, and the resting-place of the patriarchs in hope of resurrection. The plains of Mamre stand as a quiet emblem of the believer’s walk with God — a settled dwelling, an altar raised, communion with the LORD, and the sure hope of the inheritance that lies beyond the grave.

Webster 1828 Definition

The oaks or plains by Hebron where Abram dwelt and built an altar, and where the LORD appeared to him; named for an Amorite ally.

expand to see more

MAMRE, the oaks or plains by Hebron where Abram pitched his tent and built an altar (Gen 13:18).

Named for Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and Aner, confederate with Abram (Gen 14:13).

The place where the LORD appeared to Abraham in the heat of the day (Gen 18:1).

Near the field and cave of Machpelah, the patriarchs’ burying-place (Gen 23:17).

Where Jacob came to Isaac his father before Isaac’s death (Gen 35:27).

Key Scripture

Gen 13:18 — "Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar unto the LORD."

Gen 18:1 — "And the LORD appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre: and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day;"

Gen 23:19 — "And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan."

Gen 14:13 — "And there came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Hebrew; for he dwelt in the plain of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner: and these were confederate with Abram."

Modern Corruption

The lesson to recover is the pattern of the believer’s walk: a settled altar, communion with God, and hope beyond the grave.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Mamre gathers up the marks of a life lived with God. Abram dwelt there and built an altar; there the LORD appeared and renewed His promise; and nearby the patriarchs were laid to rest in hope. The place is a portrait of faith at rest in the covenant, not restless and wandering but settled in worship and fellowship with the living God.

The believer finds in Mamre an enduring example. Abraham’s hospitality to the three men, his intercession for Sodom that followed, and his purchase of Machpelah as a pledge of the promised land — all flowed from communion with God in that quiet place. So the saints are called to raise the altar of worship, to walk in fellowship with their Lord, and to bury their dead in the sure hope of the resurrection promised in the everlasting covenant.

Hebrew Roots

The name is read as “strength” or “fatness,” borne by an Amorite ally and given to the grove and plain by Hebron.

expand to see more

Mamre — from Hebrew, perhaps “strength” or “fatness, vigor.”

First the name of an Amorite, brother of Eshcol and Aner (Gen 14:24).

Transferred to the oaks or terebinths where Abram dwelt.

Identified in Scripture with Hebron in the land of Canaan (Gen 23:19).

The site of patriarchal altar, theophany, and burial alike (Gen 49:30).

Usage

"Abram removed his tent and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, building an altar there."

"In the plains of Mamre the LORD appeared to Abraham at his tent door."

"Sarah was buried in the cave of Machpelah before Mamre, which is Hebron."
